canonical_data: per-question search graphs, searcher transcripts, and reference maps held by the server process; no durable store
current_repo_note: Research prototype from the 2024 MindSearch paper with a deployed demo on the maintainers' own platform; the last push to the default branch was in July 2025.
strengths: Decomposes a question into a graph of sub-queries that searcher agents answer in parallel, then writes the answer with numbered references mapped back to source URLs
Runs fully self-hosted with an open InternLM model served locally, or with OpenAI, Qwen, or SiliconFlow-hosted endpoints, and five interchangeable search engines
Ships a FastAPI backend plus React, Gradio, and Streamlit front ends and a terminal debug mode, so a reader can run it end to end
weaknesses: No push to the default branch since July 2025, and the README documents no release process or versioning
The planner writes code that the server executes to build the graph, and the README documents no approval step or sandbox for it
Answer quality depends on a small local model by default; the maintainers' own accuracy claims sit in the paper rather than in a reproducible harness in the repository
why_it_matters: The best-known open implementation of a planner-and-searchers deep-search design, useful as a self-hostable reference for graph-structured web research.
